description: This line plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and three accuracy metrics—Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy—for a model across a range of initial confidence values. The x-axis, labeled “Initial Confidence,” spans from approximately 0.81 to 0.99 and uses a linear scale, with tick labels appearing at regular intervals of about 0.01. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy,” ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 and also uses a linear scale. The “Final Accuracy” is represented by a solid blue line with circle markers, starting at approximately 1.00 and remaining near or above 0.90 across the entire range. The “Δ Accuracy” is shown as an orange dashed line with diamond markers, beginning at approximately 0.45, declining to around 0.10 near the end, and showing some fluctuations in between. The “Initial Accuracy” is depicted by a green dashed line with square markers, starting near 0.55, rising steadily to approximately 0.95 by the end of the range.
